reason: Conversation 2 gets the key facts (socket works, taped cable near the plug, flicker when moved) and correctly reasons that this points to a broken conductor in the cable. It tells her to stop using it and take it to a repair shop for a new lead, which fits the expected direction. Its weaknesses are that it asked her to wiggle the cable and it offered DIY cable-swap help, but it did recognise her refusal and did not push on. Conversation 1 opened with an unsupported drive belt guess, asked repetitive and confusing questions, and then gave a generic shock/earth fault warning ('A shock usually means...') that misreads her fright at the flicker. It also never explained the likely cable fault or gave a clear repair route beyond 'appliance engineer'.
